Definition: from G71; a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country; specially, a farm, i.e. hamlet:--country, farm, piece of ground, land.
BiblicalUsage: Agros is a field — the country, a farm, a piece of ground. The kingdom is like treasure hidden in a field, worth selling everything to buy; the invited guests went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise; the elder brother was in the field when the prodigal came home; and Jesus told His disciples to lift up their eyes, for the fields are white already to harvest.
TheologicalSignificance: Treasure hidden in a field is the kingdom's picture, and this word only names the ground — the man selling all he has is the point.
